rappel_detail.anchor: slung rock horn or a fixed ring on webbing
rappel_detail.station: The head of the central gully on the summit pyramid, below the short summit-block downclimb.
rappel_detail.notes: First of one to three short gully rappels on a single 30-60 m rope; more rappelling later in the season as the snow melts out.
hazards: The gully is a rockfall corridor, especially with several parties in it.

rappel_detail.anchor: slung horn, fixed station or occasionally a picket
rappel_detail.station: A lower station in the central gully.
rappel_detail.notes: Down to the base of the summit pyramid; some parties make only one gully rappel and downclimb the rest, others need a third. Then descend Hell's Highway onto the Upper Curtis Glacier and traverse west.

rappel_detail.anchor: picket in snow or ice (bring your own)
rappel_detail.station: The top of Winnie's Slide, on the way back west toward the White Salmon Glacier.
rappel_detail.notes: Optional: a single rappel of about 30 m, rigged only when the slope is icy; otherwise downclimb facing in.
hazards: Pickets left by earlier parties are often pulled by later ones.

set.rappels: About 3: one to three short rappels down the summit pyramid gully, plus an optional rappel of about 30 m at Winnie's Slide if icy
set.rappel_count_note: The summit pyramid gully takes one to three short rappels depending on snow cover, and Winnie's Slide needs one of about 30 m only when icy. The table lists two gully rappels and the Winnie's Slide rappel, a typical total of three. Gully rappel lengths are not published.
set.descent: Rappel and downclimb the summit pyramid gully, descend Hell's Highway to the Upper Curtis Glacier, then go west down Winnie's Slide and the White Salmon Glacier.
